claim: For the specified one-dimensional harmonic mean-field Langevin particle system with iid initial vectors of finite covariance, the empirical mean fluctuation has exact N^(1/2) scaling and covariance governed by the 2x2 Lyapunov equation C'=AC+CA^T+sigma^2 e2 e2^T.
full_quantifiers: For every N>=1, gamma>0, omega>0, sigma>0, kappa in R, and iid Z_0^i in R^2 with mean m_0 and covariance Sigma_0, define A=[[0,1],[-(omega^2-kappa),-gamma]]. Then G_N=sqrt(N)(M_N-m) solves dG_N=AG_N dt+sigma e_2 dW_N exactly, and Cov(G_N(t))=C(t) for all t>=0, where C(0)=Sigma_0 and C'=AC+CA^T+sigma^2 e_2e_2^T. For finite fourth initial moment, the associated finite-test empirical fluctuation field converges in C([0,T]) for every fixed T<infinity and finite family of compactly supported smooth tests to the Gaussian weak SPDE specified in RESULT.txt.
supplied_inputs: N, gamma, omega, kappa, sigma, iid initial law; independent Brownian motions.
proof: Summing the particle equations gives the exact mean SDE. The standard iid vector CLT gives the initial Gaussian fluctuation; the normalized sum of Brownian motions is standard Brownian. Matrix Itô gives the covariance ODE. For the finite-test field, synchronously couple particles to iid nonlinear copies, represent the interaction as a common linear shift, apply the iid functional CLT to finitely many test processes, and Taylor-expand smooth tests. The empirical weak equation has a quadratic remainder of order N^(-1/2) times a tight product on each fixed horizon.
costs: 2x2 matrix exponential/Lyapunov calculation; one global mean and O(N) local drift arithmetic per numerical time step. Exact-real analysis only; no parameter acquisition or discretization error is claimed.
matched_baseline: The iid nonlinear copies driven by the same initial samples and Brownian motions and the supplied deterministic mean path.
falsifier: An exact solution contradicting the summed mean SDE, covariance integral, or weak test covariance equation under the stated model and moments.

claim: If both the centered kinetic matrix A_0 and mean matrix A are Hurwitz, the expected error for each fixed 1-Lipschitz observable is O(N^(-1/2)) uniformly over all t>=0, with an explicit constant.
full_quantifiers: For every fixed gamma>0, omega>0, sigma>0, kappa<omega^2, iid initial Z_0 with finite covariance Sigma_0, every N>=1, every deterministic f:R^2->R with Lip(f)<=1, and every t>=0, choose M_0,M_A>=1 and rho_0,rho_A>0 such that ||e^(A_0t)||<=M_0e^(-rho_0t) and ||e^(At)||<=M_Ae^(-rho_At). Set K=M_0^2(tr(Sigma_0)+sigma^2/(2rho_0)). Then E|mu_t^N(f)-mu_t(f)| <= sqrt(K)(1+|kappa|M_A/rho_A)/sqrt(N). The same constant bounds sup_{t>=0}sup_{Lip(f)<=1} E|mu_t^N(f)-mu_t(f)|; it is not a bound on E[W_1].
supplied_inputs: Stable model parameters and iid initial law with finite covariance.
proof: The centered nonlinear copies have uniformly bounded second moment K. Their sample mean deviation Y_N has L2 norm at most sqrt(K/N). The common particle-to-copy shift solves Delta'=A Delta+kappa e2 Y_N^x. Semigroup decay and Minkowski yield ||Delta||_L2<=|kappa|M_A sqrt(K)/(rho_A sqrt(N)). The iid empirical sampling term for each 1-Lipschitz f has expected absolute value at most sqrt(K/N).
costs: The displayed constant depends on semigroup decay and nonnormal conditioning. It becomes large near a zero eigenvalue. No entropy, log-Sobolev, or oracle cost is charged.
matched_baseline: Iid nonlinear copies with the same information and noise; their sampling contribution is explicitly separated from the common interaction shift.
falsifier: For a stable parameter choice, an exact evaluation of the left side exceeding the stated right side refutes the bound.

primary_sources.title: Uniform-in-time estimates on corrections to mean field for interacting Brownian particles
primary_sources.comparison: Theorem 1.4 proves an all-t>=0 scalar-test quantitative Gaussian CLT for a nearby smooth kinetic Langevin class, at d2 rate C0(N^(-1/2)+e^(-lambda0 t)N^(-1/3)); Remark 1.5 gives O(N^(-1/2)) uniformly when the normalized noise-free test variance stays uniformly nondegenerate. This is scalar at each time, not measure-valued path convergence. The model here is a closed-form special case; priority remains UNKNOWN.

unresolved_gate: Sharp dependence of the all-time constant on the gap near criticality; extension to nonlinear/singular interactions and to expected Wasserstein distance.
novelty: UNKNOWN; scoped exact bound for a linear model, not a general propagation-of-chaos advance.

claim: A uniform-in-time O(N^(-1/2)) hydrodynamic error holds for every interaction strength, including critical and unstable mean modes.
full_quantifiers: False already in the model of KFL-1. For critical kappa=omega^2, gamma,sigma>0 and deterministic iid initial data Z_0^i=(0,0), Var(m_N^x(t)-m_t^x)=sigma^2/(gamma^2N)[t-2(1-e^(-gamma t))/gamma+(1-e^(-2gamma t))/(2gamma)]. At t=cN this tends to sigma^2c/gamma^2. For unstable kappa>omega^2, put q=kappa-omega^2 and r=(-gamma+sqrt(gamma^2+4q))/2>0; for l=(r+gamma,1), Var(l dot (m_N-m_t))=sigma^2(e^(2rt)-1)/(2rN), which is order one at t=(log N)/(2r)+s.
supplied_inputs: The same exact harmonic Langevin system; deterministic zero initial condition; sigma>0.
proof: At criticality, solve the velocity OU mode and integrate it once to obtain the position variance. In the unstable case, project the exact mean SDE onto a left eigenvector with eigenvalue r and solve the resulting scalar unstable OU equation.
costs: Closed-form 2x2 linear SDE calculation; no numerical or oracle cost.
matched_baseline: The deterministic McKean-Vlasov mean m_t, which is identically zero for the counterexamples.
falsifier: The closed-form variances can be checked directly by Itô calculus; either variance failing at its stated horizon would falsify this counterexample.

claim: Primary fluctuation results establish finite-horizon Gaussian empirical-field CLTs for general McKean-Vlasov diffusions and for a recent class of degenerate kinetic McKean-Vlasov equations, under topology- and interaction-specific assumptions; critical models can require different scaling and non-Gaussian limits.
full_quantifiers: Fernández-Méléard (1997) report weighted negative Sobolev OU-field convergence for their stated model class on finite horizons. Hao-Zhang-Zhao (2026-07-15), Theorem 4.5, assume iid initial data, b=0, time-independent K, beta in (1,2), K in K_beta intersect B^(beta-2,infinity)_(2;a), |K|^2 in K_0, and mu_0 in B^(2d+1,infinity)_(1;a) intersect B^(2d+1,infinity)_(2;a), and prove finite-horizon convergence in C([0,T];B^(alpha-3,2)_(2;a,ell-1)) for every ell<0 and alpha<-2d. Their Theorem 4.10 gives a smooth-test expectation bound C N^(-1/2) uniformly in t in [0,T]. Dawson (1983) reports a non-Gaussian critical fluctuation regime for a mean-field oscillator model.
supplied_inputs: Primary publisher or arXiv records and source text/abstract as linked.
proof: These are source-reported published/preprint theorems, not proofs reconstructed in this leaf. The kinetic paper states the assumptions and theorem explicitly in its v1 HTML; its CLT uses additional regularity beyond its separate entropy propagation result.
costs: The kinetic CLT has topology-specific anisotropic Besov regularity and finite-horizon constants; Theorem 4.10 constants depend on T, test family, K, and mu_0. The path-space entropy theorem separately requires entropic-chaotic initial data. No uniform-in-infinite-time conclusion is claimed by these cited CLTs.
matched_baseline: The finite-horizon gaussian fluctuation/SPDE results are matched on empirical-measure scale and linearized noise; Dawson is a critical-regime contrast.
falsifier: A primary-source theorem/hypothesis contradicting the stated quantifiers, topology, or date; full independent proof audit remains open.

claim: A uniform-in-time quantitative Gaussian CLT for each smooth scalar test is already established for a small-coupling smooth kinetic Langevin class, but this does not establish full measure-valued process convergence.
full_quantifiers: Bernou-Duerinckx, Theorem 1.4 (arXiv:2405.19306v4 dated 2025-02-16; submitted 2024-05-29): for dimension d>=1, the Langevin model dX_i=V_i dt, dV_i=-(kappa/N)sum_j grad W(X_i-X_j)dt-(beta/2)V_i dt-grad A(X_i)dt+dB_i with beta>0, W smooth bounded and even, A(x)=a|x|^2/2 with a>0, iid initial law mu_0 satisfying integral exp(|z|^theta)mu_0(dz)<infinity for some theta>0, there are lambda_0,kappa_0>0 depending only on d,beta,W,A,theta such that for 0<=kappa<=kappa_0, all N>=1, t>=0, and phi in C_c^infinity(R^(2d), there is C_0 depending only on d,beta,W,A,mu_0 with d_2(sqrt(N) integral phi(d mu_t^N-d mu_t), integral phi d nu_t)<=C_0(N^(-1/2)+exp(-lambda_0 t)N^(-1/3))||phi||_(W^(4,infinity))^2. Here nu_t is the centered Gaussian linearized Dean-Kawasaki fluctuation field and d_2 is the second-order Zolotarev metric on scalar laws defined in the source. Remark 1.5 supplies an improved bound O(N^(-1/2)) when c_t(phi)=||phi||_(W^(2,infinity))^(-2)Var[integral phi d tilde-nu_t] is bounded below uniformly in t, where tilde-nu is the initial-fluctuation-only linearized field. The theorem is for each test and each time, uniformly in the bound; it does not provide convergence of the empirical fluctuation process in a full measure-valued path topology or a supremum over the test class.
supplied_inputs: Primary paper, model parameters, iid stretched-exponential initial law, smooth even W, quadratic confinement, positive beta, and small nonnegative kappa.
proof: Source theorem, not reconstructed in this leaf. The paper derives uniform-time ergodic estimates for the linearized Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation using hypocoercivity and combines these with Lions expansions and Stein’s method. No entropy-chaotic initial assumption or log-Sobolev premise is stated for Theorem 1.4; the decay estimate is established under the stated small-coupling and confinement assumptions. Direct applicability to the exact model in KFL-1 is not claimed: its unbounded mean-force interaction does not meet the paper’s stated smooth bounded pair-potential hypothesis.
costs: The theorem states existence of lambda_0,kappa_0,C_0 with dependencies rather than numerical values. Its proof uses smoothness, stretched-exponential moment control, small coupling, and a hypocoercive ergodic estimate. No computational cost is reported.
matched_baseline: The empirical measure of the interacting kinetic Langevin system compared with the scalar projection of its Gaussian linearized Dean-Kawasaki limit.
falsifier: A mismatch between the quoted theorem statement and arXiv:2405.19306v4 Theorem 1.4/Remark 1.5, or a counterexample satisfying all its assumptions and violating the stated scalar d2 bound.
